title: The Signal Garden
author: Barış Kısır
premise: Biophysicist Mira Voss builds an illegal research station deep in the Norwegian spruce forest to study a fungus that seems to remember — and answer — the dying calls of trees. When a salvage drone returns with soil holding a signal that matches the station's own encryption, Mira and her estranged brother have 72 hours to decode a forest that is talking to itself.
short_description: A mycologist exiled for her unorthodox theories discovers the forest is answering her research station's own encryption — and has 72 hours to decode it before the burn order lands.
long_description: 2043. Dr. Mira Voss was expelled from academia for her papers on mycelial memory; now she listens to a spruce forest from a one-room station in northern Norway, built in an old logging barracks. When her estranged brother Leo — ex-military comms engineer, now a salvage drone pilot — chases a crashed drone to the same coordinates, the soil there carries a signal encoded with Mira's own key. Twenty years ago she planted that grove as her dissertation. Now the forest is answering. As the Agency's burn-and-seed order closes in, Mira and Leo must hold the fire line long enough to decode a message written across forty kilometers of root network — a question the forest has been waiting a generation to ask.
main_characters: Dr. Mira Voss — biophysicist, exiled for her mycelial memory papers
Leo Voss — her estranged brother, ex-military comms engineer, salvage drone pilot
Dr. Hanne Ruud — grizzled regional ecologist, ally
Agent Falk — Agency enforcer with a soft spot for trees
Runa — Mira's daughter, at university, appears by voice-call
The Groves — the fungus, a character: sets, signals, memory
